raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Part of #43304: CPU counters currently merge tokenizer/detokenizer workers with the same `component`, hiding per-worker load skew.

## Modifications

Add a `pid` label to the shared CPU counter and bind its child once per monitor thread. CPU delta calculation, sampling interval and launch paths remain unchanged. This applies consistently to all existing monitor callers.

This changes metric cardinality: queries expecting one series per component need `sum without (pid)`. PIDs identify process lifetimes rather than stable worker slots; exited-worker counter values remain until the multiprocess directory is cleared. These tradeoffs and example queries are documented. Processing-time and queue-latency metrics are outside this PR.

## Accuracy Tests

- **Direct regression coverage:** all 3 CPU-monitor tests pass on macOS arm64/Python 3.12.14. The two-subprocess regression fails against original production code (1 merged series instead of 2), then passes with the change. It waits for monitor initialization, uses process CPU time for its workload and waits for a positive sample.
- **Linux compatibility:** an isolated import of the production monitor on Linux arm64/Python 3.12.14 with `prometheus-client==0.20.0` (the declared minimum) produces distinct PID series and preserves the sum reported by the individual processes. This checks the monitor/collector, not a full SGLang deployment.
- **HTTP export:** two real subprocesses, the production `add_prometheus_middleware`, FastAPI/Uvicorn and an HTTP GET to `/metrics` yield two PID series distinguishing a busy process from an idle one.
- 9 neighboring metrics-utils tests also pass; these are not additional coverage of the changed behavior.

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python .venv/bin/python -m pytest test/registered/unit/observability/test_cpu_monitor.py -q
PYTHONPATH=python .venv/bin/python test/registered/unit/observability/test_cpu_monitor.py -v
```

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No serving-speed improvement is claimed. No model inference or complete serving benchmark was run.

## Checklist

- [x] Configured pre-commit checks pass for the three changed files.
- [x] Regression coverage is in the existing registered CPU-monitor test file.
- [x] Metric compatibility and queries are documented.
- [x] Mintlify build validation and link/anchor/redirect checks pass.

AI assistance: implemented and tested with Codex. Human/upstream review is pending. This PR is ready for review; upstream functional CI has not yet been validated.

@@ -7,6 +7,24 @@ SGLang exposes the following metrics via Prometheus. You can enable it by adding
 
 An example of the monitoring dashboard is available in [examples/monitoring/grafana.json](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/examples/monitoring/grafana/dashboards/json/sglang-dashboard.json).
 
+## Process CPU usage
+
+With `--enable-metrics`, `sglang:process_cpu_seconds_total` accumulates user and system CPU seconds, sampled every five seconds. The `component` label identifies `tokenizer`, `detokenizer`, `detokenizer_router`, or `data_parallel_controller`. The `pid` label identifies the process, so workers of the same component remain distinguishable in multiprocess collection.
+
+To compare tokenizer workers within each scraped server instance:
+
+```promql
+rate(sglang:process_cpu_seconds_total{component="tokenizer"}[1m])
+```
+
+A value of `1` means one CPU core on average. To aggregate workers by component while keeping server instances separate:
+
+```promql
+sum without (pid) (rate(sglang:process_cpu_seconds_total[1m]))
+```
+
+Queries that previously expected one series per component must now aggregate across `pid`. A PID identifies a process rather than a stable worker slot; worker restarts can create new series. Multiprocess counter files retain exited workers' last values until the metrics directory is cleared on server restart, so use rates to compare CPU usage rather than cumulative totals.
+
 ## Language model metrics
 
 `sglang:time_to_first_token_seconds` measures the time from request creation in the API server to the first token. For streaming requests it ends when the first output arrives after detokenization, which may contain no printable text. Non-streaming clients only see the final response, so for them it ends when the scheduler produced the first token.

+
+start_cpu_monitor_thread("tokenizer", interval=0.01)
+deadline = time.monotonic() + 10
+while cpu_total() is None:
+    assert time.monotonic() < deadline, "CPU monitor did not initialize"
+    time.sleep(0.01)
+target_cpu_time = time.process_time() + 0.1
+while time.process_time() < target_cpu_time:
+    sum(i * i for i in range(1000))
+deadline = time.monotonic() + 10
+while cpu_total() <= 0:
+    assert time.monotonic() < deadline, "CPU monitor did not sample CPU usage"
+    time.sleep(0.01)
+print(os.getpid())
+"""
+        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
+            env = {**os.environ, "PROMETHEUS_MULTIPROC_DIR": directory}
+            workers = [

+                    env=env,
+                    stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
+                    stderr=subprocess.PIPE,

+            ]
+            pids = set()

+                    pids.add(stdout.strip().splitlines()[-1])
+
+                registry = CollectorRegistry()
+                multiprocess.MultiProcessCollector(registry, path=directory)
+                samples = [

+                    for metric in registry.collect()
+                    for sample in metric.samples
